// why: The reference input of the negative control: a minimal but WHOLE repository, in which every tracked file is reached from a root. Every case beside it is built on a copy of this one and brings in exactly one defect, so a case file holds the defect alone rather than one more copy of a correct input. Were this reference itself defective, every case would fire because of it — which is why the gate checks it separately.
// files: Sixteen files covering the five ways a file is reached at once: from a root (`package.json`), by a path in a configuration (`vendor.json`), by a pattern in `inputs` (`src/button.scss`), by an import with the extension left off (`./button` in `src/index.ts`), by a bare unique name (`guide.md` in the README) and through the two grants that are not names — the fixtures tree of `check-widget.mjs`, and the `vendor` tree of the register. `assets/logo.png` is binary: it has no entry in `texts`, mentions nothing and still has to be reached.

texts.README.md: The plan is in docs/plan.md, the shape of a page in guide.md, and the mark in assets/logo.png.
texts.docs/guide.md: How a page is written. Points nowhere further.
texts.docs/plan.md: The task list. Points nowhere further.
texts.vendor/skills/build/SKILL.md: The steps of the build live in notes.md.

roots.reason: npm reads the manifest by name — the entry point of everything else here.
The task runner enumerates project configurations by this name.
The front page: rendered by name, pointed at by nothing inside.

enumerated.reason: The outside tool walks its own tree and finds a skill by the shape of the directory, so no path to those files is ever written down here.
